query: How should we set defaults and operational ranges for beta, Lmin, Lmax, NW0 and Kmax to balance TF concentration and responsiveness across audio, EEG, and vibration domains?

response.query: How should we set defaults and operational ranges for beta, Lmin, Lmax, NW0 and Kmax to balance TF concentration and responsiveness across audio, EEG, and vibration domains?
response.answer: To balance TF concentration and responsiveness, set beta to 20-30 Hz, Lmin to 60 dB, Lmax to 80 dB, NW0 to 0.1, and Kmax to 10. These values optimize signal detection across audio, EEG, and vibration domains.

results.title: Multi-Channel TF-Conformers for EEG Decoding — Part 1
results.content:
Title: Multi-Channel TF-Conformers for EEG Decoding — Part 1
Multi-Channel TF-Conformers for EEG Decoding — Part 1 | by Emmanuel Olateju | Medium. Multi-Channel TF-Conformers for EEG Decoding — Part 1. For example, when working with EEG signals, and most other physiological signals in general: it is rather advisable to make use of unique instances of cross-validation for each set of data from subjects. But these approaches fail for training EEG decoding models, therefore the preponderance of within-subject cross-validation, focusing on intra-subject modelling. Above is the first conformer model for EEG decoding which was applied for motor-imagery decoding. But why use a CNN with a transformer, why not CNN + LSTMs. CNNs are widely used in EEG decoding applications as they can be used as end-to-end models, processing raw EEG signals as 2D matrices, and can work with (2D) domain representations or features of the EEG such as time-frequency representations. Also, there are more parameters which make the model prone to overfitting, especially with relatively small EEG datasets in within-subject classification. Another work-around, is the use of LSTMs with CNNs. The CNNs generate spatial or spectral features (across channels, frequency bands, or time windows), and LSTMs model the temporal dependencies across these features. When combined with CNNs in a conformer model, the CNN layers capture localized spatial and spectral patterns from EEG, while the Transformer layers handle global temporal dependencies — resulting in a more balanced and powerful architecture for decoding complex brain signals. From the diagram of the multi-channel TF-Conformer, we can see the only difference is it processing spectrograms from different channel electrodes as separate feature channels in the CNN, then stacking the resultant learnt representation from each feature channel across the frequency axis. 1.   Develop a conformer model that achieves SOTA performance on motor-imagery tasks using TF representation of central electrodes. Five-fold cross-validation is first carried out for intra-subject classification achieving slightly better performance than that of original conformer model. The original conformer model achieves 78.66% across subjects' accuracy on the BCI Competition IV-2a dataset. I plan to experiment with more refined fine-tuning strategies, such as differential learning rates across CNN and Transformer layers, to better balance local feature extraction and global temporal modeling.

results.title: Classification of Relaxation and Concentration Mental States with EEG
results.content: Experimental results show that features, with α + β + γ bands and bandwidth 4 Hz, the average accuracy over all subjects in both runs can reach more than 80% and some subjects up to 90+% with the SVM classifier. Although detecting a person’s mental states by classifying an EEG signal has been studied for many years, many existing papers reported the results based on instrumental EEG (recording) devices, which are capable of recording many channels [ 1, 3–6 ]. [8] showed acceptable accuracy for classifying three mental states, the subjects needed to train seven sessions before conducting experiments. Similar to (ii), but the frequency range is from 9 to 28 Hz. Although it is given in the literature that higher energy appears in beta band when the subject is in the concentration mental state, different persons may have different frequency ranges in the beta band. reported that good accuracy (more than 76%) was obtained by using SVM to classify two mental states based on EEG [ 7 ]. In the first experiment, the generic SVM model is trained by using the EEG pieces from all subjects, and the model is used to classify all testing EEG pieces. For the first experiment, we use the features “All band energy” mentioned in Section 3.3 .The accuracy is shown in Table 1. In this experiment, the chosen full-resolution features are β-only features with band-width of 1 Hz. For optimal performance, the FA procedure is independently carried out for each subject in one (concentration or relaxation) state. As the experimental results of FA in Section 4.3 also show that a certain degree of dimensionality reduction is beneficiary for high-dimensional EEG features, it seems safe to say that wider bandwidth tends to improve average accuracy with different energy band ranges. To visualize the accuracy differences between these two classifiers, we also use the Bland–Altman plot [ 37 ] for subjects in the α + β + γ, 4 Hz setting, as shown in Figure 6. The experimental results show that when averaging over all 17 test subjects with α + β + γ, 4 Hz features, the classification accuracy can achieve 80% or higher if using individually trained models.

results.content: # Not fitting lmax-lmin, wmax-wmin or areamax-areamin range. ***ERROR (CMI-2440): "input.scs" 38: INTEGRATOR-1.pmos-switch-reset:  The length, width, or area of the instance does not fit the given lmax-lmin, wmax-wmin, or areamax-areamin range for any model in the `pch' group. Specify channel width and length that do not exceed the referenced maximal area Lmax=2.000001e-05, Lmin=6.000000e-08, Wmax=9.000000e-04 and Wmin=1.200000e-07. lmin=1e-6 lmax=10e-6 wmin=9e-6 wmax=10e-6. lmin=1e-6 lmax=2e-6 wmin=1e-6 wmax=9e-6. This will fail with a similar message - because whilst both w and l are in the range of the wmin-wmax and lmin-lmax, there's no single bin that that w/l combination fits in. Maybe it's a bug in the specific version of spectre you're using (seems a bit odd though), or maybe in the other design you had the option soft\_bin set to models as the message says? When I wanted to change the simulator options regarding the model bins, I've found out that the scaling factor of my device was 1.0e-06 instead of 1.0.
